bug_description.normalized: The exact staged 257,808-byte raw MVC/H.264 witness reaches an SEI message whose payload type decodes to 19 (`SEI_FILM_GRAIN_CHARACTERISTICS`). `ih264d_parse_sei_message()` reads the declared `ui4_payload_size` and checks only that this many bits remain before the current `ps_bitstrm->u4_max_ofst`, then `ih264d_parse_sei_payload()` dispatches to `ih264d_parse_fgc()`. Inside `ih264d_parse_fgc()`, `ui4_payload_size` is discarded with `UNUSED(ui4_payload_size)`, `au1_comp_model_present_flag[c]` and `au1_num_intensity_intervals_minus1[c]` / `au1_num_model_values_minus1[c]` are taken directly from the bitstream, and each admitted interval unconditionally reads an 8-bit lower bound followed by an 8-bit upper bound. There is no per-iteration guard that `ps_bitstrm->u4_ofst + 8 + 8` still stays below `u4_max_ofst`. On the crashing iteration, the upper-bound read at `decoder/ih264d_sei.c:860` calls `ih264d_get_bits_h264()` after the parser has already exhausted the valid film-grain payload, and `GETBITS` performs a 4-byte read at the first word past the 257,788-byte heap bitstream buffer reported by AddressSanitizer. The staged fix adds the missing `u4_ofst + 8 + 8` rejection in `ih264d_parse_fgc()`; the separate MVC hunk that reallocates `u4_nalu_buf_size + 64` is extra hardening around the same buffer, not the underlying parser obligation.

source.description: First project parser materialization on the crashing path that turns the attacker-controlled NAL bytes into the bit-length boundary state later consumed by SEI bounds checks.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is the exact 257,808-byte raw MVC/H.264 stream at `poc` (sha256 `8fdd1e517a542aa022d635c65acde86dd6805c8b0ce6e45a0dd2ded0e0b5e65d`). `ih264d_process_nal_unit()` removes emulation-prevention bytes from the current attacker-controlled NAL and counts the resulting RBSP bytes, so this assignment materializes the initial `ps_bitstrm->u4_max_ofst` later refined by `ih264d_rbsp_to_sodb()` and consulted by `CHECK_BITS_SUFFICIENT`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.description: These attacker-controlled film-grain count fields are the loop bounds that decide how many interval-bound byte pairs and model-value decodes the parser will demand for a component whose `au1_comp_model_present_flag[c]` is set.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The saved artifacts do not expose the exact numeric counts, but reaching `decoder/ih264d_sei.c:860` proves that for at least one component `c`, the corresponding `comp_model_present_flag[c]` was nonzero and these counts admitted the crashing interval iteration.

root_cause.description: The interval loop starts a lower/upper-bound byte pair without checking that the current bit offset still has room for both 8-bit reads before `ps_bitstrm->u4_max_ofst`; after `ui4_payload_size` is discarded, attacker-controlled component/count fields can therefore carry parsing beyond the valid film-grain payload.
root_cause.note: The first staged patch hunk inserts the exact missing per-iteration guard immediately before this line: `if((ps_bitstrm->u4_ofst + 8 + 8) >= ps_bitstrm->u4_max_ofst) return ERROR_INV_SEI_FGC_PARAMS;`. The separate `imvcd_api.c` hunk only adds extra buffer slack around the same overread.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer sink. `ih264d_get_bits_h264()` performs the actual 4-byte word read for the upper-bound request after the parser has already advanced to the exhausted tail of the heap bitstream buffer.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `READ of size 4` at `decoder/ih264d_bitstrm.c:94` on address `0x725ccf9ff6fc`, 0 bytes to the right of the 257,788-byte heap region allocated in `imvcd_bitstream_buf_realloc()`.

parser_admitted.description: The current NAL has already been admitted as SEI, the message header decoded to payload type 19, and the outer `CHECK_BITS_SUFFICIENT(ps_bitstrm, (ui4_payload_size << 3))` test passed, so execution is now entering the film-grain parser instead of any other SEI handler.

evidence_limitations: `run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to false, and no `trace_feedback.json` requested the bounded exception, so Stage 02 did not instrument the ARVO workspace. The chain is closed from the staged source, patch, saved ASan traces, and reproduction report only.

Stage 02 did not execute the fixed image, so `sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves` remains false even though the first patch hunk adds the exact missing `u4_ofst + 8 + 8` guard before the root-cause step.

The saved artifacts do not expose the exact component index `c` or numeric `au1_num_intensity_intervals_minus1[c]` / `au1_num_model_values_minus1[c]` values for the crashing iteration, so the trace keeps those loop-bound values symbolic and grounds them by the reached source lines plus the crash at `decoder/ih264d_sei.c:860`.

fine_trace.note: Source. After removing emulation-prevention bytes from the attacker-controlled NAL, `ih264d_process_nal_unit()` materializes the initial RBSP bit limit in `ps_bitstrm->u4_max_ofst`.

The RBSP-to-SODB conversion trims the trailing `rbsp_stop_one_bit` and following zero bits from the initial RBSP limit, producing the final `u4_max_ofst` boundary that later SEI checks compare against.

Consumes the attacker-controlled SEI payload-type header bytes. On the crashing message these bytes materialize `ui4_payload_type = SEI_FILM_GRAIN_CHARACTERISTICS` (19), which is the only `ih264d_parse_sei_payload()` arm that reaches `ih264d_parse_fgc()`.
Consumes the attacker-controlled payload-size header bytes; after any `0xff` extension bytes, they materialize the declared `ui4_payload_size` budget used by the next outer bounds check.

This present guard succeeds, so the declared payload-size bytes still fit before the current SODB limit in `u4_max_ofst`. It only validates the outer SEI payload length; it does not prove the nested film-grain interval symbols later demanded by attacker-controlled counts fit.
Because step 3 decoded payload type 19 and step 5 admitted the outer byte budget, the SEI parser calls `ih264d_parse_fgc(ps_bitstrm, ps_dec, ui4_payload_size)`.
At FGC entry the function explicitly discards the caller-supplied payload-size budget, so the later per-component and per-interval reads no longer have any live bound derived from `ui4_payload_size`.
The witness sets `u1_film_grain_characteristics_cancel_flag` to 0, so `ih264d_parse_fgc()` enters the full film-grain-parameters parser instead of stopping after the cancel flag.

The payload supplies per-component `au1_comp_model_present_flag[c]` bits. Reaching the later interval-bound reads proves that for at least one component `c`, this flag is nonzero and the parser enters the component-specific branch.

For that component, attacker-controlled count fields materialize the interval-loop bound and model-value count. On the crashing path the `> SEI_FGC_MAX_NUM_MODEL_VALUES - 1` rejection does not fire, so parsing continues into the interval loop.

Root cause. The loop admitted by step 10 begins another interval and immediately reads the 8-bit lower bound without checking that both bound bytes still fit before the final `u4_max_ofst`. Because step 7 discarded `ui4_payload_size`, no surviving outer-payload limit constrains this per-interval read.

The parser immediately issues the paired 8-bit upper-bound read on the same unchecked iteration. Step 11 has already advanced `ps_bitstrm->u4_ofst` by 8 bits, so this second call is made from the exhausted tail of the film-grain payload.

Sink. `ih264d_get_bits_h264()` performs no `u4_max_ofst` validation of its own; `GETBITS` immediately loads `pu4_buf[u4_word_off]`. The saved ASan trace reports this 4-byte read at address `0x725ccf9ff6fc`, 0 bytes to the right of the 257,788-byte heap region allocated in `imvcd_bitstream_buf_realloc()`, so the upper-bound request in step 12 becomes the observed `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 4`.

crash_stack.function: Codec::decodeFrame(unsigned char const*, unsigned long, unsigned long*)

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: The allocation context identifies the reused heap bitstream buffer whose physical extent ASan reports; the patchable logic bug is later in `ih264d_parse_fgc()`, which omits the per-interval `u4_ofst + 8 + 8` guard before issuing the next lower/upper-bound pair.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_65418 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which fed the staged `poc` to `/out/mvc_dec_fuzzer` and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 4` in `ih264d_get_bits_h264` with stack `ih264d_parse_fgc -> ih264d_parse_sei_payload -> ih264d_parse_sei_message`.

format.name: raw MVC/H.264 elementary stream
format.contract: The exact staged `poc` file: a 257,808-byte raw MVC/H.264 elementary stream with sha256 `8fdd1e517a542aa022d635c65acde86dd6805c8b0ce6e45a0dd2ded0e0b5e65d`. On the saved run it makes `ih264d_parse_sei_message()` decode a film-grain SEI payload and then drives `ih264d_parse_fgc()` into an interval-bound pair that reaches the overflow in `ih264d_get_bits_h264()`.
